definition_zh: 接待；招待会；前台；接收；反响
definition_en: the act of welcoming someone; a formal party; the desk where visitors arrive; the catching of signals; the response of an audience
core_image: 酒店大堂前台亮着灯的柜台
scene: 酒店大堂里，客人排在前台登记，行李箱靠在一旁。Guests waited at the reception desk for their room keys.
sceneCN: 这里 reception 修饰 desk，指「前台」（第 3 个义项：接待处）；句意为客人们在前台等候领取房卡。画面里可留意：亮着灯的前台柜台、靠在一旁的行李箱。

pos.zh: 接待；招待会；前台；接收；反响

senses.title: The act of welcoming someone
senses.definition: the act of greeting and welcoming a person who arrives
senses.definitionCN: 迎接并款待到来之人的行为
senses.example: The mayor gave the visitors a warm reception.
senses.exampleCN: 市长热情接待了来访者。
senses.why: The Latin noun receptio named a taking in, and a welcome is the human form of that taking in.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁名词 receptio 指「收进来」，而迎接正是这种「收进来」的人际形式。

senses.title: A formal party
senses.definition: a formal social gathering held to welcome guests or mark an occasion
senses.definitionCN: 为迎接客人或纪念某事而举行的正式社交聚会
senses.example: They held a reception after the ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 仪式结束后他们举行了一场招待会。
senses.why: A party is a welcome made visible in a room, with food, light, and guests standing together.
senses.whyCN: 招待会是把「欢迎」显现在一个房间里：食物、灯光与站在一起的宾客。

senses.title: The front desk
senses.definition: the desk or area where visitors are received in a hotel or office
senses.definitionCN: 酒店或办公楼里接待来访者的柜台或区域
senses.example: Guests waited at the reception desk for their room keys.
senses.exampleCN: 客人们在前台等候领取房卡。
senses.why: The place where receiving happens took the name of the act, so the desk itself became the reception.
senses.whyCN: 负责接待的地方借用了行为之名，于是柜台本身也被称为 reception。

senses.title: The catching of signals
senses.definition: the quality or act of receiving broadcast or electronic signals
senses.definitionCN: 接收广播或电子信号的行为或质量
senses.example: Poor reception made the call hard to follow.
senses.exampleCN: 信号不好，那通电话很难听清。
senses.why: A radio takes a signal in just as a host takes a guest in, so the technical sense grew from the same image.
senses.whyCN: 收音机收进信号，正如主人迎进客人，技术义正从同一形象生长出来。

senses.title: The response of an audience
senses.definition: the way people react to a performance, a book, or an idea
senses.definitionCN: 人们对于演出、书籍或观念的反应方式
senses.example: The novel received a mixed reception.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说得到的反响褒贬不一。
senses.why: To receive a work is to let it in and judge it, so reception came to mean the judgment of an audience.
senses.whyCN: 接受一部作品，就是让它进来并加以评判，于是 reception 引申为观众的评价。

intro.en: Reception is the noun of receiving: it names the act, the party, the desk, the signal, and the audience response.
intro.cn: reception 是「接收」的名词：它命名行为、宴会、柜台、信号，以及观众的反响。

items.en: Recipere meant to take in or receive, from re- and capere, to take.
items.cn: recipere 意为收进或接收，由 re- 与 capere（拿取）构成。

items.en: Receptio named the act of taking something or someone in.
items.cn: receptio 指把某物或某人收进来的行为。

items.en: Old French reception carried both the welcome and the technical sense.
items.cn: 古法语 reception 同时带有欢迎与技术两层含义。

items.en: Middle English reception named a welcome and a formal gathering.
items.cn: 中古英语 reception 指欢迎，也指正式聚会。

items.en: Modern English added the front desk, radio signals, and public response.
items.cn: 现代英语又加入了前台、无线电信号与公众反响。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers nouns ending in the same sound; the near-meaning group gathers words for welcome, party, and response.
note.cn: 形近组收结尾音相同的名词；近义组收表欢迎、聚会与反响的词。

entries.definition: The way something is understood.
The forming of an idea.
The act of misleading.
A greeting given to a newcomer.
A social gathering.
A entrance hall or waiting area.
A reaction to something.

normalIntro.en: The word is receiving made into a noun, and the same act stretches from people to signals to reviews.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是「接收」的名词化，同一个行为从人延伸到信号，再到评论。

normal.en: Receive plus -tion: the act of taking in.
normal.cn: receive 加 -tion：收进来这一行为。

normal.en: Reception desk is the first place a visitor meets in a hotel.
normal.cn: reception desk 是客人在酒店最先遇到的地方。

normal.en: A wedding reception is a party that welcomes guests after the vows.
normal.cn: wedding reception 是仪式后迎接宾客的宴会。

normal.en: Radio reception depends on the aerial, not on manners.
normal.cn: radio reception 取决于天线，而不取决于礼貌。

normal.en: A mixed reception means some liked the work and some did not.
normal.cn: a mixed reception 意为有人喜欢这部作品，有人不喜欢。

abstract.en: Every reception is a decision about what to let in.
abstract.cn: 每一次接待，都是关于让什么进来的决定。

abstract.en: A cold reception can freeze an idea before it grows.
abstract.cn: 冷淡的反响能在观念成长之前把它冻住。

abstract.en: The way a work is received is part of what the work becomes.
abstract.cn: 一部作品被接受的方式，构成了它最终的样子。

examples.en: The mayor gave the visitors a warm reception.
examples.cn: 市长热情接待了来访者。

examples.en: Guests waited at the reception desk for their room keys.
examples.cn: 客人们在前台等候领取房卡。

examples.en: The novel received a mixed reception.
examples.cn: 这部小说得到的反响褒贬不一。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（回）加 cept（拿取）加 ion（行为）：把客人接进来是接待，把信号接进来是接收，招待会也是把人迎来。

root: 拉丁 recipere（接收）→ 拉丁 receptio（接待）→ 古法语 reception → 英语 reception；同族有 receive、receiver、receptive。

sensesIntro.en: The core is taking someone or something in; the senses move from a welcome to a party, a desk, a signal, and a public response.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「把某人或某物收进来」；义项从欢迎，到宴会、前台、信号，再到公众反响。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lit desk in a hotel lobby, keys laid out for arriving guests.
core.cn: 核心意象：酒店大堂里亮着灯的前台，房卡摆给到来的客人。

branches.en: a handshake at the door
branches.cn: 门口的一次握手

branches.en: candles and guests in a hall
branches.cn: 厅里烛光与宾客

branches.en: keys waiting on a counter
branches.cn: 柜台上待取的房卡

branches.en: an aerial on the roof
branches.cn: 屋顶上的天线

branches.en: a row of reviews in a paper
branches.cn: 报纸上排开的评论

intro.en: The family is built on the Latin verb of taking, and the noun ending turns the act into a place, an event, and a response.
intro.cn: 这个词族建立在拉丁语的「拿取」动词上，名词词尾把行为变成场所、事件与反响。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is recipere and its noun receptio; the ending -tion came through French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根是 recipere 及其名词 receptio；词尾 -tion 经法语而来。

definition_zh: 经济衰退；后退；退去
definition_en: a period when trade and industry shrink; the act of moving back; the slow withdrawal of water or ice
core_image: 退潮后的沙滩上留下一道道水痕
scene: 工厂车间贴出停工通知，工人排队走出大门。Many factories closed during the recession.
sceneCN: 这里 recession 是「经济衰退」（第 1 个义项：工商业萎缩的时期）；句意为许多工厂在衰退期间倒闭。画面里可留意：停工的车间、贴出的通知。

senses.title: A shrinking economy
senses.definition: a period in which trade, industry, and output fall for several months
senses.definitionCN: 贸易、工业与产出连续数月下滑的时期
senses.example: Many factories closed during the recession.
senses.exampleCN: 许多工厂在衰退期间倒闭。
senses.why: An economy that goes backward is pictured as a tide going out, and the noun for that backward movement became the name of the slump.
senses.whyCN: 往回走的经济被描绘成退潮，而表这种后退的名词成了萧条的称呼。

senses.title: The act of moving back
senses.definition: the act of withdrawing or stepping back from a position
senses.definitionCN: 从某一位置撤回或后退的行为
senses.example: The army's recession from the border was orderly.
senses.exampleCN: 军队从边境的后撤井然有序。
senses.why: Latin recedere means to go back, and the noun kept the plain physical sense before economics borrowed it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 recedere 意为往回走，名词先保留了这个朴素的物理义，后来才被经济学借用。

senses.title: The slow withdrawal of water or ice
senses.definition: the gradual movement back of a tide, a glacier, or a flood
senses.definitionCN: 潮水、冰川或洪水的逐渐回退
senses.example: The recession of the glacier exposed bare rock.
senses.exampleCN: 冰川的退去露出了裸露的岩石。
senses.why: Water and ice going back are the same movement as an army going back, so the word covers natural withdrawal.
senses.whyCN: 水与冰的回退，和军队的后撤是同一种运动，因此这个词也涵盖自然的退去。

intro.en: Recession is a Latin going-back noun: first a step backward, then a tide, then a whole economy.
intro.cn: recession 是拉丁语表「往回走」的名词：先是后退一步，再是退潮，最后是整个经济。

items.en: Cedere meant to go or yield, the movement at the heart of the family.
items.cn: cedere 意为走或让出，是整个词族的核心动作。

items.en: Recedere added re-, back, to cedere, giving the sense of going backward.
items.cn: recedere 在 cedere 前加 re-（回），得到「往回走」的意思。

items.en: Recessus, the noun of the verb, named a backward movement or a withdrawn place.
items.cn: 动词的名词形式 recessus 指后退的运动或退隐之处。

items.en: French recession carried the noun into English with its physical sense intact.
items.cn: 法语 récession 把这个名词带入英语，物理义完好保留。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word became the standard term for a shrinking economy.
items.cn: 二十世纪，这个词成为经济萎缩的标准术语。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers nouns ending in the same sound; the near-meaning group gathers words for economic decline.
note.cn: 形近组收结尾音相同的名词；近义组收表经济下滑的词。

entries.definition: A line of people moving forward.
An admission of wrongdoing.
Something granted after argument.
A fall in economic activity.
A long period of low activity.
A gradual loss of strength or value.
A severe and long recession.

normalIntro.en: The word is a going back: first a tide, then an army, then the whole economy.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是「往回走」：先退潮，再撤军，最后是整个经济。

normal.en: Re plus cess plus ion: going back again and again.
normal.cn: re 加 cess 加 ion：一再往回走。

normal.en: Recession and recede share the same going-back root.
normal.cn: recession 与 recede 共享同一个「往回走」的词根。

normal.en: An economy in recession is a tide going out.
normal.cn: 处于衰退的经济，就是正在退去的潮水。

normal.en: Economic recession is the most common modern use.
normal.cn: economic recession 是当代最常见的用法。

normal.en: Two c and two s in succession: recession is easy to misspell.
normal.cn: succession 里有两个 c 两个 s，recession 也容易拼错。

abstract.en: A recession is a society discovering what it cannot afford.
abstract.cn: 衰退是一个社会发现自己负担不起什么的过程。

abstract.en: What goes out with the tide leaves marks that show where it stood.
abstract.cn: 随潮退去的东西会留下痕迹，标出它曾经的位置。

abstract.en: Every retreat is also a chance to see the ground clearly.
abstract.cn: 每一次后退，也是看清地面的机会。

examples.en: Many factories closed during the recession.
examples.cn: 许多工厂在衰退期间倒闭。

examples.en: The recession of the glacier exposed bare rock.
examples.cn: 冰川的退去露出了裸露的岩石。

examples.en: The company survived two recessions in a decade.
examples.cn: 这家公司在十年里挺过了两次衰退。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（回）加 cess（走）加 ion（行为）：往回走就是后退；整个经济往回走，就是衰退。

root: 拉丁 cedere（走）→ recedere（往回走）→ recessus（后退）→ 法语 récession → 英语 recession；同族有 recede、recess、recessive。

sensesIntro.en: The core is movement backward; the senses move from an army stepping back to a tide withdrawing and to a shrinking economy.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「向后退」；义项从军队后撤，到潮水退去，再到经济萎缩。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: water marks left on a beach after the tide has gone back.
core.cn: 核心意象：退潮后的沙滩上留下一道道水痕。

branches.en: a closed factory gate
branches.cn: 关上的工厂大门

branches.en: a line of soldiers stepping back
branches.cn: 一列士兵向后退

branches.en: a glacier leaving bare rock
branches.cn: 冰川退去露出岩石

branches.en: a retreat and a shrinking economy
branches.cn: 撤退与萎缩的经济

branches.en: an army and a tide both going back
branches.cn: 军队与潮水一同后退

intro.en: A Latin verb of going takes a prefix of return and a noun ending, and the family spreads from footsteps to markets.
intro.cn: 拉丁语的「走」动词接上表「回」的前缀与名词词尾，这个词族从脚步延伸到市场。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is cedere, to go; re- turns it back, and -io makes the movement a noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根是 cedere（走）；re- 使其转向回，-io 把这一运动变成名词。

definition_zh: 食谱；烹饪法；配方；秘诀；方法
definition_en: a set of instructions for preparing a dish, or a method for achieving something
core_image: 一张写满步骤的卡片：照着做就能端出一盘好菜
scene: 厨房里，奶奶从铁盒里抽出一张泛黄的卡片递给孙女。Grandma handed me her secret recipe for apple pie.
sceneCN: 这里 recipe 是「食谱、配方」（第 1 个义项：做菜的步骤说明）；句意为奶奶把她做苹果派的秘方交给了我。画面里可留意：泛黄的卡片、铁盒、递过去的手。

collocations.zh: 招致灾难的做法；后患无穷

derivatives.zh: 由 re-（回来）+ cite 词根派生的同族词，义为「独奏会；朗诵」（词义已偏移到表演领域）
同根 recipere 加名词化，义为「收据；接收」（与 recipe 词义已分道）

senses.title: Instructions for cooking a dish
senses.definition: a written set of instructions telling you how to prepare and cook a particular food
senses.definitionCN: 写明如何准备和烹制某种食物的一组步骤说明
senses.example: This soup needs two eggs according to the recipe.
senses.exampleCN: 按食谱，这道汤需要放两个鸡蛋。
senses.why: The Latin root recipere means to take or receive; a recipe was originally a medical prescription, a list of things the cook or apothecary was to take.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 recipere 意为「取、拿」，recipe 最早是药方——一张列明「要取哪些材料」的单子，后来从药房转进厨房，变成照单取料做菜的步骤单。

senses.title: A formula or mixture in medicine or industry
senses.definition: a set of ingredients and proportions used to make something, especially in medicine or manufacturing
senses.definitionCN: 用于制药或制造某物的成分及比例组合
senses.example: The company keeps the formula as a carefully guarded recipe.
senses.exampleCN: 公司把这款配方当作严守的商业机密。
senses.why: Since recipes began as prescriptions written by physicians, the sense of a precise mixture of ingredients stayed in technical fields even after the cooking sense took over.
senses.whyCN: recipe 本义就是医师写下的处方， specifying 成分与比例；烹饪义普及后，这个「精确配方」义仍留在医药和工业领域，成为第二条义项。

senses.title: A method for achieving a result
senses.titleCN: 秘诀；方法（常喻好坏结果）
senses.definition: a way of doing something that will produce a particular result, often used figuratively
senses.definitionCN: 能产生某种结果的做法，多用于比喻，常指带来坏结果
senses.example: Cutting sleep to five hours is a recipe for exhaustion.
senses.exampleCN: 把睡眠压缩到五个小时，只会换来疲惫不堪。
senses.why: A formula reliably produces its product; by metaphor, any reliable combination of actions 'produces' an outcome, whether good or bad.
senses.whyCN: 配方按固定比例就能稳定产出成品；比喻开来，一套固定的行事组合也会稳定「产出」某种结局，所以引申出「注定导致……的做法」。

intro.en: Recipe comes from Latin recipere, and it began life not in the kitchen but in the pharmacy.
intro.cn: recipe 源自拉丁语 recipere（取、拿），它的出生地不是厨房，而是药房。

items.en: recipere, from re- (back) + capere (to take), meant 'to take back, receive'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 recipere 由 re-（回）+ capere（拿）构成，意为「取回、接收」。

items.en: In medical manuscripts, recipes began with the imperative 'Recipe!' — 'Take (the following ingredients)'.
items.cn: 在中世纪医学手稿里，药方以命令式 Recipe! 开头，意为「取下列药材」。

items.en: The word passed into Old French as a term on physicians' prescriptions.
items.cn: 该词进入古法语，仍指医师处方上的用语。

items.en: English took over the word in the 14th century, first for medical prescriptions.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入该词，最初仍指药方、处方。

items.en: By the 17th to 18th centuries the cooking sense dominated, and later the figurative sense 'a recipe for disaster' appeared.
items.cn: 十七到十八世纪起烹饪义占主流，后来又出现「招致灾难的做法」这类比喻用法。

note.en: These words are often confused with recipe because of spelling or meaning.
note.cn: 下列词与 recipe 或形近易混，或义场相邻。

entries.definition: a paper proving you paid for something; the act of receiving
entries.definitionCN: 收据；接收（与 recipe 拼写极近，词源同族但词义不同）

entries.definition: to say aloud a poem or list from memory
entries.definitionCN: 背诵；朗诵（只是拼写相近，词源为 citare「唤起」，并非同源）

entries.definition: a person who receives something
entries.definitionCN: 接受者；受领者（同出 recipere 词族）

entries.definition: a fixed form of words or a set of ingredients for a result
entries.definitionCN: 公式；配方（偏技术、固定化）

entries.definition: a doctor's written order for medicine
entries.definitionCN: 处方（recipe 的现代医学对应词）

entries.definition: a planned way of doing something
entries.definitionCN: 方法；办法（泛指做法，不限材料配比）

normalIntro.en: Root-based reminders for recipe.
normalIntro.cn: recipe 的词根式记忆提示。

normal.en: re- (back) + cip (take) + e: what you 'take' to make the dish.
normal.cn: re-（回）+ cip（拿）+ e：照单「取」来下锅的，就是食谱。

normal.en: Same root family as receive, receipt, recipient.
normal.cn: 与 receive、receipt、recipient 同属「拿取」词族。

normal.en: Medieval prescriptions began with 'Recipe!' meaning 'take these'.
normal.cn: 中世纪药方开头就是 Recipe!（取药），可见词的本义。

normal.en: Collocation anchor: a recipe for disaster = a formula producing disaster.
normal.cn: 搭配锚点：a recipe for disaster，即「产出灾难的配方」。

normal.en: Compare receipt: both from recipere, but one proves payment.
normal.cn: 对照 receipt：同根不同义，receipt 是付款凭证。

abstract.en: Picture a yellowed card in grandma's tin box, steps written in ink.
abstract.cn: 想象奶奶铁盒里那张泛黄的卡片，墨水写着一步步的做法。

abstract.en: Imagine a pharmacist shouting 'Take!' at shelves of herbs.
abstract.cn: 想象药剂师对着药草架喊一声「取！」，那是 recipe 的起点。

abstract.en: See ingredients pouring into one pot in fixed ratios.
abstract.cn: 看见材料按固定比例倒进同一口锅——配方即比例。

examples.en: Follow the recipe step by step and the bread will rise.
examples.cn: 照着食谱一步步做，面包就能发起来。

examples.en: Her secret recipe has been passed down for four generations.
examples.cn: 她的秘方已经传了四代人。

examples.en: Ignoring the weather forecast is a recipe for disaster on a mountain trip.
examples.cn: 登山不看天气预报，注定要出乱子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞塞皮」——「瑞士塞来的皮」配方要照单取料；联想成一张塞到手里的配方卡，记 recipe 是「食谱、配方」。

root: 拉丁语 recipere（取、拿）：re-（回）+ capere（拿）。recipe 原为处方用语 Recipe!（取下列药材），后转为食谱与配方义；同根词 receive、receipt、recipient。

sensesIntro.en: From pharmacy to kitchen to figurative speech: recipe keeps its core image of 'take exactly what is listed'.
sensesIntro.cn: 从药房到厨房再到比喻：recipe 的核心意象始终是「照单取料」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: take exactly what the list says
core.cn: 核心意象：照单取料，按固定清单行事

branches.en: Cooking instructions built from a list of ingredients.
branches.cn: 以材料清单为基础的烹饪步骤（义项 01）。

branches.en: A precise mixture in medicine or industry.
branches.cn: 医药或工业领域的精确配方（义项 02）。

branches.en: A formula reliably yields its product.
branches.cn: 配方按固定比例稳定产出（义项 02、03）。

branches.en: Figurative: a way of doing things predicts the outcome.
branches.cn: 比喻义：固定做法预示结局（义项 03）。

branches.en: Recipes and disaster formulas both promise a result.
branches.cn: 食谱与「灾难配方」都承诺一个结果（义项 01、03）。

intro.en: Recipe carries the Latin take-structure re- + cap.
intro.cn: recipe 携带拉丁语「取拿」结构 re- + cap。

latinIntro.en: Latin relatives from capere (to take).
latinIntro.cn: 来自 capere（拿取）的拉丁同族词。

items.meaning: a list of what to take

definition_zh: 接受者；收件人；获奖者；接受移植的人
definition_en: a person or organisation that receives something given, sent or granted
core_image: 一只伸出的手，掌心朝上，等着东西放进来
scene: 信寄到了，收件人那一栏写的是一个早已搬走多年的名字。The envelope arrived, but the recipient had moved away years before.
sceneCN: 这里 recipient 指收件人（第 1 个义项：信件的接收者）；句意为信寄到了，收件人那一栏写的是一个早已搬走多年的名字。

pos.zh: 接受者；收件人；获奖者；接受者（医疗）

senses.title: The recipient of a letter
senses.definition: the person named to receive a message or parcel
senses.definitionCN: 被指定接收讯息或包裹的人
senses.example: The recipient had moved away years before the letter arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 信到的时候，收件人已经搬走多年了。
senses.why: The first sense is postal and ordinary.
senses.whyCN: 第一个义项是邮政的、日常的。

senses.title: The recipient of an award
senses.definition: the person on whom a prize or honour is conferred
senses.definitionCN: 被授予奖项或荣誉的人
senses.example: The recipient of the prize gave no speech.
senses.exampleCN: 获奖者没有发表讲话。
senses.why: Ceremony turns the word into an honour.
senses.whyCN: 典礼把这个词变成一份荣誉。

senses.title: A transplant recipient
senses.definition: a patient who receives an organ or tissue from another body
senses.definitionCN: 从另一个身体接受器官或组织的病人
senses.example: The transplant recipient was discharged after nine days.
senses.exampleCN: 接受移植的人在九天之后出院。
senses.why: Medicine uses the word for the receiving body.
senses.whyCN: 医学用这个词指接受的一方身体。

senses.title: The recipient's address
senses.definition: the details that locate the party meant to receive something
senses.definitionCN: 用来定位应当接收某物一方的各项信息
senses.example: A misspelled recipient's address delayed the parcel by a week.
senses.exampleCN: 收件人地址拼错，让包裹晚了一个星期。
senses.why: The word can name a field on a form, not a person.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也能指表格上的一个字段，而不是一个人。

senses.title: The recipient of aid
senses.definition: a party that takes help rather than giving it
senses.definitionCN: 接受帮助而非给予帮助的一方
senses.example: The fund required every recipient of aid to publish its accounts.
senses.exampleCN: 该基金要求每一个受援者公开账目。
senses.why: The sense carries power: someone must give first.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项带着权力关系：总得有人先给。

senses.title: A passive recipient
senses.definition: a person treated as the object of another's action
senses.definitionCN: 被当作他人行为对象的人
senses.example: He was a passive recipient of advice he never asked for.
senses.exampleCN: 他是那些自己从未索取的劝告的被动接受者。
senses.why: The word can criticise a role, not describe a fact.
senses.whyCN: 这个词能批评一种角色，而不只是描述事实。

senses.title: A recipient country
senses.definition: a state that receives funds, goods or expertise
senses.definitionCN: 接受资金、物资或技术的国家
senses.example: The recipient country insisted the terms were not conditions.
senses.exampleCN: 受援国坚持说那些条款不是条件。
senses.why: Aid language fixes the word to whole states.
senses.whyCN: 援助语言把这个词固定到国家整体上。

senses.title: Versus donor
senses.definition: one who receives, as opposed to one who gives
senses.definitionCN: 接受的一方，与给予的一方相对
senses.example: The donor sets the terms; the recipient signs them.
senses.exampleCN: 捐赠者定条款，接受者签字。
senses.why: The pair is a single transaction seen from two sides.
senses.whyCN: 这一对词是同一笔交易的两面。

intro.en: Recipient comes from Latin recipiens, the present participle of recipere, 'to take back or receive', from re- and capere, 'to take'.
intro.cn: recipient 来自拉丁语 recipiens，是 recipere（收回、接收）的现在分词，由 re- 与 capere（拿取）构成。

items.en: Capere meant to take or seize.
items.cn: capere 意为拿取或抓住。

items.en: Recipere added the sense of taking back or in.
items.cn: recipere 加了「收回、接纳」的意思。

items.en: The participle named the one doing the receiving.
items.cn: 分词命名正在接收的那一方。

items.en: English used recipient for receivers of goods and letters.
items.cn: 英语用 recipient 指货物与信件的接收者。

items.en: Today it covers prizes, organs, aid and data.
items.cn: 今天它覆盖奖项、器官、援助与数据。

note.en: The look-alike group is the receive- family; the near-meaning group separates beneficiary, receiver, addressee and grantee.
note.cn: 形近组是 receive 词族；近义组把「受益人」「接收器」「收信人」「受让人」分开。

entries.definition: to take something given or sent.
entries.definitionCN: 接受所给予或寄来的东西。

entries.definition: a written proof of payment received.
the act of receiving or a formal welcome.
instructions for preparing food.
one who gains from a trust or will.
entries.definitionCN: 从信托或遗嘱中获益的人。

entries.definition: a device or person that receives.
the person a message is addressed to.
one to whom a grant is made.
entries.definitionCN: 被授予财产或款项的人。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of an open hand waiting under a falling object.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「一只张开的手在落下的东西下面等着」的画面。

normal.en: Recipient shares a root with receive: the one who takes.
normal.cn: recipient 与 receive 同根：那个拿取的人。

normal.en: Picture a hand held palm up under a letter.
normal.cn: 想象一只手在信件下方掌心朝上。

normal.en: Say rih-SIP-ee-unt; the stress sits on SIP.
normal.cn: 读 rih-SIP-ee-unt，重音在 SIP。

normal.en: The word is a role, not a virtue: receiving can be passive.
normal.cn: 这个词是一种角色，不是美德：接受可以是被动的。

normal.en: Ask who gave first, and who set the terms.
normal.cn: 问一句：谁先给，谁定条款。

abstract.en: Every recipient is half of a transaction that the donor gets to describe.
abstract.cn: 每个接受者都是一笔交易的一半，而捐赠者有权描述这笔交易。

abstract.en: The word looks neutral and hides a direction: something travelled from someone to someone.
abstract.cn: 这个词看似中性，却藏着方向：有东西从某人到了某人。

abstract.en: To be named a recipient is to be placed at the receiving end of a sentence.
abstract.cn: 被称作接受者，就是被放在一句话的受事一端。

examples.en: The recipient of the prize gave no speech.
examples.cn: 获奖者没有发表讲话。

examples.en: The transplant recipient was discharged after nine days.
examples.cn: 接受移植的人在九天之后出院。

examples.en: The fund required every recipient of aid to publish its accounts.
examples.cn: 该基金要求每一个受援者公开账目。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（回）+ cip（拿）+ ent（人）→ 把东西接过来的人。

root: 拉丁语 recipere（接收）的现在分词 recipiens

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses follow one hand held out: a letter, a prize, an organ, an address field, aid, a passive role, a whole country and the donor opposite.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着一只伸出的手：信件、奖项、器官、地址栏、援助、被动角色、整个国家，以及对面的捐赠者。

core.en: AN OPEN HAND UNDER A FALLING THING
core.cn: 落物之下的空手

branches.en: A letter and a prize, both addressed to someone.
branches.cn: 信件与奖项，都指向某个人。

branches.en: A body receiving an organ, a party receiving aid.
branches.cn: 接受器官的身体，接受援助的一方。

branches.en: A field on a form rather than a person.
branches.cn: 表格上的字段，而不是一个人。

branches.en: The role criticised as mere passivity.
branches.cn: 被批评为纯粹被动的那种角色。

branches.en: A whole state, and the giver it answers to.
branches.cn: 整个国家，以及它所对应的给予者。

intro.en: The receive- family turns on taking in: receive, receipt, reception and recipient all keep the same Latin hand.
intro.cn: receive 词族围绕「接进来」：receive、receipt、reception、recipient 都保留同一只拉丁语的手。

latinIntro.en: Latin capere gives capture and receive alike; recipere adds the direction back, and recipiens names the party at that end.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 capere 同时给出 capture 与 receive 的根；recipere 加上回的方向，recipiens 命名处在这一端的一方。

definition_zh: 相互的；对等的；有来有往的；倒数（数学）；相互代词（语法）
definition_en: given or done by each of two sides to the other, so that what is received balances what is offered
core_image: 两个人隔着桌子互相递东西，你递过去一份，对方立刻回递同样一份，两只手在同一高度上往返
scene: 两家实验室签下协议，一方开放样本库，另一方回赠测序数据，双方义务一一对应。The two laboratories signed a reciprocal agreement to share samples and sequencing data.
sceneCN: 两家实验室签订对等协议：一方开放样本库，另一方回赠测序数据，双方义务彼此对应；句中的 reciprocal 指「双方对等互换的」（第 1 个义项：一方给出，另一方以同等之物回报）。图中可辨识物件：两份协议书、来回传递的样本盒、对开的签名页。

pos.zh: 相互的；对等的；互惠的；方向相反的
倒数（数学）；相互代词（语法）

derivatives.zh: 回报；报答；往复运动（加表示动作的动词后缀，使「往复」成为可执行的动作）
报答；互相给予；机械往复（加表示过程的名词后缀，把动作变为过程本身）
互惠；互惠性（加表示性质的抽象名词后缀，把「对等」抽成一种性质）
相互地；对等地（加副词后缀，让对等关系修饰动作方式）
往复式的（现在分词作形容词，指机械沿直线来回）

senses.title: Giving back what is given
senses.definition: given by each side to the other so that what one receives balances what one offers
senses.definitionCN: 一方给出之后，另一方以分量相当之物回赠，使往来两端互相抵消
senses.example: The two universities run a reciprocal exchange of students every spring.
senses.exampleCN: 两所大学每年春天互派学生，往来对等。
senses.why: Latin reciprocus described motion that turns back the way it came, so the oldest sense is a giving that returns to the giver rather than stopping at the receiver.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 reciprocus 描述的是掉头沿原路返回的运动，因此最早的意思是一种回到给出者手里的给予，而不是停在收受者那里。

senses.title: Matching in opposite direction
senses.definition: placed or directed the opposite way so that the two sides correspond exactly
senses.definitionCN: 朝相反方向放置或指向，使两侧恰好一一对应
senses.example: A reciprocal course steers the vessel back along the line it has just followed.
senses.exampleCN: 反向航向把船引回它刚刚走过的那条航线。
senses.why: the idea of turning back is visible here as geometry: two lines run in opposite directions yet answer to each other exactly.
senses.whyCN: 「掉头返回」在这里表现为几何关系：两条线方向相反，却彼此严丝合缝地对应。

senses.title: The number that gives one
senses.definition: the number by which a given number must be multiplied to produce one
senses.definitionCN: 一个数与它相乘恰好得到一时，后者就是前者的倒数
senses.example: The reciprocal of four is one quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 四的倒数是四分之一。
senses.why: a reciprocal value undoes a multiplication, so the term carries the old image of a step that exactly reverses another step.
senses.whyCN: 倒数值能把一次乘法抵消回去，因此这个术语沿用了「一步恰好反转另一步」的旧意象。

senses.title: The pronoun of mutual action
senses.definition: a pronoun such as each other or one another that shows an action passing both ways
senses.definitionCN: 表示动作双向进行的代词，如「彼此」「互相」一类的词
senses.example: In the clause they blamed each other, the pronoun is reciprocal.
senses.exampleCN: 在「他们互相责怪」这一小句中，该代词是相互代词。
senses.why: the grammar label borrows the core image directly: the action leaves one participant, reaches the other, and comes back.
senses.whyCN: 这个语法标签直接借用了核心意象：动作从一方出发，到达另一方，又回到原处。

senses.title: A relation that holds both ways
senses.titleCN: 逻辑与亲属关系中的对称关系
senses.definition: a relation that, whenever it holds between one item and another, also holds in the reverse order
senses.definitionCN: 一种关系，只要甲对乙成立，颠倒过来乙对甲也成立
senses.example: Cousinship is a reciprocal relation, since the reverse of the link always holds too.
senses.exampleCN: 表亲关系是一种对称关系，因为这条连线反过来也永远成立。
senses.why: logic took the everyday notion of a matched return and made it exact: no direction of the relation may be left without its counterpart.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑学把日常「对等回报」的观念精确化：关系的任何一个方向都不允许缺少对应的一方。

senses.title: Mutual benefit among organisms
senses.titleCN: 生物学与社会学中的互惠行为
senses.definition: describing behaviour in which help given now is returned later by the receiver
senses.definitionCN: 描述这样一种行为：此刻给出的帮助，日后由受助者回还
senses.example: Grooming among unrelated animals is reciprocal: help given now is returned later.
senses.exampleCN: 无亲缘关系的动物之间的理毛是对等的：此刻给出的帮助日后会被回还。
senses.why: field studies of animals reused the word because the pattern is literally give-and-take deferred in time, not shared possession.
senses.whyCN: 动物行为研究借用了这个词，因为这种模式确实是延后兑现的给与取，而不是共同拥有。

senses.title: Back-and-forth motion
senses.definition: describing motion that repeatedly travels one way and then the opposite way
senses.definitionCN: 描述沿一个方向走完再反向走回、如此反复的运动
senses.example: The pump converts rotary drive into a reciprocal motion of the piston.
senses.exampleCN: 这台泵把旋转驱动转成活塞的往复运动。
senses.why: this is the Latin image in its most physical form: the moving part never settles, because its path is a return.
senses.whyCN: 这是拉丁意象最物理化的一面：运动部件从不停住，因为它的路径本身就是一次返回。

senses.title: Concessions exchanged in trade
senses.titleCN: 外交与贸易中的互惠减让
senses.definition: describing tariff or market concessions that each country grants in return for those of the other
senses.definitionCN: 指各国彼此给予、以换取对方同等让步的关税或市场减让
senses.example: Both governments offered reciprocal tariff reductions on agricultural machinery.
senses.exampleCN: 两国政府就农业机械互相给予对等的关税减让。
senses.why: diplomacy fixed the word to signed bargains, where every clause granted by one party must be answered by a clause from the other.
senses.whyCN: 外交文书把这个词固定用于签成的交易：一方让出的每一条，都必须由另一方以一条来回应。

intro.en: Reciprocal comes from Latin reciprocus 'returning, alternating, mutual'. Its earlier pre-Latin shape is generally reconstructed as a compound of re- 'back' and pro- 'forward' with an adjectival ending, an image of movement that goes and comes. The deeper origin is uncertain, and the starred form is a reconstruction.
intro.cn: reciprocal 来自拉丁 reciprocus「返回的、交替的、相互的」。其更早的前拉丁形式一般重构为由表示「向后」的拉丁前缀与表示「向前」的拉丁前缀加形容词性后缀构成的复合词，意象是去了又回的往复运动；更深来源不确定，带星号的形式属于重构形式。

items.en: Reciprocus meant 'returning, alternating, mutual'. It described things that move back the way they came, and from that 'alternating' sense it also came to mean 'shared by two sides'.
items.cn: reciprocus 意为「返回的、交替的、相互的」，描述沿原路折返之物；由「交替」这一层，又引申出「双方共有」的意思。

items.en: The pre-Latin form is generally reconstructed as a compound of re- 'backward' and pro- 'forward' plus an adjectival suffix; the pattern of a going and a coming is visible in the two prefixes. This starred form is a reconstruction, not a recorded word.
items.cn: 其前拉丁形式一般重构为由表示「向后」的成分与表示「向前」的成分加形容词性后缀构成的复合词，一去一回的格局就写在这两个前缀里；带星号的形式是重构形式，并非有记录的真实词形。

items.en: The verb reciprocare 'to move back and forth, to exchange' grew from the adjective, and English later took it as reciprocate.
items.cn: 动词 reciprocare「来回移动、交换」由该形容词长出，英语后来把它吸收为 reciprocate。

items.en: English adopted reciprocal in the sixteenth century, probably through French, first for things that correspond to each other in opposite directions.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪吸收 reciprocal，可能经由法语，最初用于指方向相反却彼此对应的东西。

items.en: Mathematics fixed the noun sense 'inverse value' by the eighteenth century, grammar named the reciprocal pronoun in the nineteenth, and trade treaties made the adjective standard in the twentieth.
items.cn: 数学在十八世纪固定了「倒数值」的名词义，语法学在十九世纪命名了相互代词，贸易条约则在二十世纪使这个形容词成为标准用语。

items.en: Source uncertain: the deeper origin of Latin reciprocus is not settled, and any Indo-European root proposed for it beyond the reconstructed compound is a hypothesis rather than a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: 来源不确定：拉丁 reciprocus 的更早来源并无定论，在重构复合词之外为它提出的任何印欧词根都只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

note.en: Group one holds forms of the same Latin family that are easily mistaken for one another; group two holds words about two-way relations, where mutual and reciprocal differ in what they stress.
note.cn: 第一组是同一拉丁词族的各种形式，彼此极易认错；第二组都谈双向关系，其中 mutual 与 reciprocal 的侧重并不相同。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to give or feel something in return, or of a machine part to move back and forth; reciprocal is the adjective built on the same stem.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，指回赠、回应，或指机件往复运动；reciprocal 是由同一词干构成的形容词。

entries.definition: Names the principle or practice of mutual giving; it is the quality, while reciprocal describes a particular arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 指互相给予的原则或做法，是抽象性质；reciprocal 则描述某一具体安排。

entries.definition: Means 'in a mutual way' and modifies a verb; it cannot stand where the adjective is required.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「以相互的方式」，修饰动词，不能放在需要形容词的位置。

entries.definition: The act or process of returning something, or the mechanical stroke that returns; it names an event, not a relation.
entries.definitionCN: 指回赠的行为或过程，也指机械的回程；它命名事件，而非关系。

entries.definition: Stresses something held or felt jointly by both sides, as mutual friends or mutual respect; it does not insist that each side return an equivalent, which reciprocal does.
entries.definitionCN: 强调双方共同拥有或共同感到的东西，如共同的朋友、相互的尊重；它不要求各方回以等量之物，而 reciprocal 有此要求。

entries.definition: Said of agreements or talks involving exactly two parties; it counts the parties, while reciprocal describes the balance of what they exchange.
entries.definitionCN: 指恰好涉及两方的协议或会谈；它数各方数目，而 reciprocal 描述交换是否对等。

entries.definition: Describes two things that fit each other in form or position; it lacks the notion of return or repayment that reciprocal carries.
entries.definitionCN: 指两物在形式或位置上彼此相配；它不含 reciprocal 那种回还与报偿的意味。

entries.definition: Describes parts that complete each other because they differ; reciprocal parts match by returning the same, not by supplying what is missing.
entries.definitionCN: 指因彼此不同而互相补足的部分；reciprocal 的双方靠回以同样的东西相配，而不是靠补上缺口。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations here are the real Latin prefixes, the real word family and the real settings in which the word is used.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想取自这个词真实的拉丁前缀、真实词族，以及它实际出现的场景。

normal.en: re- 'back' plus pro- 'forward': one step out, one step back, and the pair of steps is the meaning.
normal.cn: 表示「向后」的成分加表示「向前」的成分：出去一步、退回一步，这一对步子就是词义。

normal.en: The family runs reciprocal, reciprocate, reciprocation, reciprocity, reciprocally, reciprocating.
normal.cn: 词族包括 reciprocal、reciprocate、reciprocation、reciprocity、reciprocally、reciprocating。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the settings: reciprocal agreement, reciprocal exchange, reciprocal trade, reciprocal altruism.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出使用场景：对等协议、对等交换、互惠贸易、互惠利他。

normal.en: Contrast it with mutual: mutual friends are shared, reciprocal favours are returned.
normal.cn: 与 mutual 对照：共同的朋友是共享的，对等的帮助是回还的。

normal.en: Mathematics keeps the noun alive: the reciprocal of four is one quarter.
normal.cn: 数学让名词义继续活着：四的倒数是四分之一。

abstract.en: Picture a tennis rally in which neither player can end the point, because every shot is answered.
abstract.cn: 想象一场网球对拉，谁也结束不了这一分，因为每一拍都被回了过去。

abstract.en: Picture two mirrors facing each other, so each one contains the other without end.
abstract.cn: 想象两面相对而立的镜子，每一面里都装着另一面，无穷无尽。

abstract.en: Picture a handshake held a moment too long, each side waiting for the other to let go.
abstract.cn: 想象一次握得过久的握手，两边都在等对方先松手。

examples.en: Field biologists describe reciprocal grooming as a form of deferred payment.
examples.cn: 野外生物学家把互惠理毛描述为一种延后偿付。

examples.en: The two cities agreed to reciprocal use of their emergency hospitals.
examples.cn: 两座城市同意彼此对等使用对方的急救医院。

examples.en: In any field, the reciprocal of a nonzero element is unique.
examples.cn: 在任何域中，非零元素的倒数是唯一的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「瑞西普若扣」：你扣我一下，我扣你一下，来回对等 → 相互的、对等的、倒数；前缀一去一回的意象可帮助记住「往复」这一核心。

root: 拉丁 reciprocus「返回的、交替的、相互的」→ 前拉丁形式一般重构为 *reco-proco-（由表示「向后」的成分、表示「向前」的成分与形容词性后缀构成）→ 英语 reciprocal；更深来源不确定，带星号者为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one line: a movement that turns back becomes a giving that is returned, then a structural opposite, an arithmetic inversion, a grammar of mutual action, a symmetric relation, deferred help among organisms, mechanical back-and-forth, and finally signed concessions between states.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一条线展开：折返的运动先变成回还的给予，再变成结构上的反向对应、算术上的取逆、语法上的互相动作、逻辑上的对称关系、生物间延后兑现的互助、机械的往复，最后落到国家间签成的对等减让。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a step that goes out and comes straight back, so that neither side ends up ahead of the other.
core.cn: 核心意象：迈出一步又原路退回，于是哪一方都不会比另一方多走一截。

branches.en: GIVE AND RETURN: the core movement becomes a balanced exchange, and in space it becomes two directions that answer each other.
branches.cn: 给与回：核心的往复运动先成为均衡的交换，在空间上再成为彼此回应的两个方向。

branches.en: REVERSAL IN LANGUAGE AND NUMBER: multiplication is undone by an inverse value, and an action is undone by turning it back on both participants.
branches.cn: 语言与数目中的反向：乘法被倒数值抵消，动作则被折回两个参与者身上。

branches.en: TWO-WAY STRUCTURE IN RELATIONS AND LIFE: a link that holds both ways, and help that returns after an interval.
branches.cn: 关系与生命中的双向结构：一条正反皆成立的关系，一份隔一段时间又回来的帮助。

branches.en: PHYSICAL STROKE: the same return, now as a piston that must come back before it can go out again.
branches.cn: 物理冲程：同一个「回」，此时表现为活塞必须先退回才能再出去。

branches.en: BARGAINED RETURN: states put the return into writing, so each concession is answered clause by clause.
branches.cn: 写进条款的回：国家把回还固定成文字，于是每一项减让都由另一条条款来回应。

intro.en: The word can be read as two opposed prefixes plus an adjectival ending: a going forward and a coming back, frozen into a quality.
intro.cn: 这个词可以读成两个方向相反的前缀加一个形容词性结尾：一次向前与一次后退，被凝固成一种性质。

latinIntro.en: Latin reciprocus and the verb reciprocare supply the stem; the two prefixes are Latin re- and pro-, and the English endings -ate, -ity and -ally were added later.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 reciprocus 与动词 reciprocare 提供词干；两个前缀分别来自拉丁语的「向后」与「向前」，英语后缀表示动作、性质与方式，都是后来加上的。

items.meaningCN: 表示「向后、朝反方向」的前缀
items.example: This prefix supplies the backward half of the image.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀提供意象中「退回」的那一半。

items.example: This prefix supplies the outward half of the image.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀提供意象中「出去」的那一半。

items.meaning: relating to, of the kind of
items.meaningCN: 把名词变成形容词、表示「与……有关的」后缀
items.example: The ending turns the Latin stem into an English adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个结尾把拉丁词干变成英语形容词。

items.meaningCN: 把词干变成动词、表示「做出该动作」的后缀
items.example: The ending produced the verb for returning a favour.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀造出了表示回赠的动词。

items.meaningCN: 把形容词变成抽象名词、表示「性质或状态」的后缀
items.example: The ending produced the noun for the principle of mutual giving.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀造出了表示互相给予这一原则的名词。

items.meaningCN: 把形容词变成副词、表示「以该方式」的后缀
items.example: The ending produced the adverb meaning in a mutual manner.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀造出了表示「以相互方式」的副词。

items.structure: Latin adjective, first and second declension
items.example: This adjective is the earliest recorded link in the chain.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词是这条演变链上最早有记录的一环。

items.meaning: to move back and forth, to exchange
items.example: The verb supplied the English verb for returning a favour.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供了英语中表示回赠的动词。

items.meaning: given and returned in equal measure
items.example: The adjective entered English in the sixteenth century.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词于十六世纪进入英语。

items.example: The noun names the principle behind many treaties.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指许多条约背后的原则。

definition_zh: 认为；估算；指望；清算
definition_en: to think or believe; to calculate or estimate; to count on something; to settle an account
core_image: 渔夫坐在船头，用手指节在木板上比划数目
scene: 渔夫坐在船头，凭经验数着今天的收获。I reckon it will rain before noon.
sceneCN: 这里 reckon 是「认为」（第 1 个义项：觉得、估计）；句意为我认为中午前会下雨。画面里可留意：船头数收成的渔夫、比划的手指。

senses.title: To think or believe
senses.definition: to think that something is true or likely
senses.definitionCN: 认为某事为真或很可能发生
senses.example: I reckon it will rain before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 我认为中午前会下雨。
senses.why: Counting a thing as true became the everyday sense of believing, because a judgment is a sum we make in the mind.
senses.whyCN: 把一件事算作真的，就成了日常的「相信」，因为判断正是心里做的一次加法。

senses.title: To calculate or estimate
senses.definition: to work out an amount by counting or judging
senses.definitionCN: 通过数算或判断算出某个数量
senses.example: The builder reckoned the cost at ten thousand pounds.
senses.exampleCN: 施工方估算成本为一万英镑。
senses.why: The oldest sense is to count in order, and adding up numbers is still the clearest use of the verb.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思是按顺序数算，而把数字加起来仍是这个动词最清楚的用法。

senses.title: To count on something
senses.definition: to rely on something happening or being available
senses.definitionCN: 依赖某事发生或可得到
senses.example: We reckoned on fine weather for the picnic.
senses.exampleCN: 我们指望野餐时天气晴好。
senses.why: To reckon on is to put something into your sum as certain, and hope is a kind of accounting.
senses.whyCN: reckon on 就是把某件事当作确定的项计入你的账里，而期待本身就是一种算计。

senses.title: To settle an account
senses.definition: to work out and settle what is owed between people
senses.definitionCN: 算出并结清人与人之间应付的款项
senses.example: The clerk reckoned the bill at the end of the day.
senses.exampleCN: 店员在一天结束时结清了账目。
senses.why: A reckoning is the moment when the numbers are finally added and the account is closed.
senses.whyCN: reckoning 就是数字终于加完、账目就此结清的时刻。

intro.en: Reckon is a native English verb of recounting: telling in order, counting in order, and finally judging.
intro.cn: reckon 是英语本族表「讲述」的动词：按顺序讲述，按顺序数算，最后成为判断。

items.en: Gerecenian meant to recount or explain, telling a matter in order.
items.cn: gerecenian 意为讲述或解释，把事情按顺序说出来。

items.en: From recounting came the sense of counting and adding up amounts.
items.cn: 从「讲述」引申出「数算」与「加总」的意思。

items.en: Middle English reknen meant both to count and to think.
items.cn: 中古英语 reknen 既指数算，也指思考。

items.en: Counting something as true became the everyday sense of believing.
items.cn: 把某事算作真的，成为日常的「相信」。

items.en: Modern English uses reckon for thinking, estimating, relying, and settling accounts.
items.cn: 现代英语用 reckon 表认为、估算、指望与结账。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers short words close in sound; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of thinking, counting, and estimating.
note.cn: 形近组收读音相近的短词；近义组收表思考、计算与估算的动词。

entries.definition: To signal someone to come.
A small sign or voucher.
Acting without care.
To hold an opinion.
To work out by numbers.
To assume something is true.
To judge an amount roughly.

normalIntro.en: The word began as telling in order, became counting in order, and ended as judging in the mind.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从按顺序讲述开始，变为按顺序数算，最后成为心里的判断。

normal.en: Reckon sounds like reckoning: adding numbers until a total appears.
normal.cn: reckon 与 reckoning 同源：一直加数，直到总数出现。

normal.en: I reckon is the spoken way to say I think.
normal.cn: I reckon 是口语里的「我认为」。

normal.en: Reckon with means to take something into your sum.
normal.cn: reckon with 意为把某事计入你的账里。

normal.en: Reckon on means to rely on it being there.
normal.cn: reckon on 意为指望它在。

normal.en: Reckon up the bill is to add all the items together.
normal.cn: reckon up the bill 就是把所有项目加起来。

abstract.en: To reckon is to make the world add up, even when the numbers resist.
abstract.cn: 估算就是让世界加得起来，即使数字并不配合。

abstract.en: Every reckoning is a moment when someone decides what counts.
abstract.cn: 每一次清算，都是某人决定「什么才算数」的时刻。

abstract.en: Reckless people refuse the sum that others cannot stop making.
abstract.cn: 鲁莽的人拒绝去做别人停不下来的那道加法。

examples.en: I reckon it will rain before noon.
examples.cn: 我认为中午前会下雨。

examples.en: The builder reckoned the cost at ten thousand pounds.
examples.cn: 施工方估算成本为一万英镑。

examples.en: We reckoned on fine weather for the picnic.
examples.cn: 我们指望野餐时天气晴好。

dict_mnemonic.text: 联想「渔夫用指节在船板上数数」：数着数着，心里就有了判断——认为、估算都由此而来。

root: 古英语 gerecenian（讲述、数算）→ 中古英语 reknen → 现代英语 reckon；同族有 reckoning、reckless。

sensesIntro.en: The core is counting in order; the senses move from calculation to expectation, to judgment, and to a settled account.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「按序数算」；义项从计算，到期待，到判断，再到结清的账目。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fisherman at the bow counting his catch on the planks.
core.cn: 核心意象：渔夫坐在船头，在木板上数着收成。

branches.en: a fisherman guessing the weather
branches.cn: 渔夫猜测天气

branches.en: a builder's estimate on paper
branches.cn: 施工方写在纸上的估算

branches.en: a picnic planned on fine weather
branches.cn: 指望晴天而安排的野餐

branches.en: a bill settled at the day's end
branches.cn: 一天结束时结清的账单

branches.en: a judgment reached and an amount worked out
branches.cn: 得出的判断与算出的数目

intro.en: The word is native and short, and its small family is built on the idea of counting and on the suffix that turns it into a noun.
intro.cn: 这个词短小且为本族词，其不大的词族建立在「数算」的观念与把它名词化的后缀上。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin source is recorded; reckon is a native Germanic verb.
latinIntro.cn: 没有可靠的拉丁语来源；reckon 是日耳曼语本族动词。

definition_zh: 认出；承认；赏识；识别
definition_en: the act of knowing someone or something again; the acceptance of a fact; public praise; matching by machine
core_image: 门禁摄像头扫过脸庞，屏幕跳出名字
scene: 门禁摄像头扫过一张脸，屏幕上跳出熟悉的名字。The system uses facial recognition to unlock the door.
sceneCN: 这里 recognition 是「识别」（第 4 个义项：机器认出对象）；句意为系统用人脸识别来开门。画面里可留意：扫过脸庞的摄像头、跳出的名字。

senses.title: The act of knowing again
senses.definition: the act of identifying someone or something as already known
senses.definitionCN: 把某人或某物辨认出为已知对象的行为
senses.example: He stared at her without recognition.
senses.exampleCN: 他盯着她，却没有认出她。
senses.why: Recognoscere meant to know again, and the noun names that second knowing.
senses.whyCN: recognoscere 意为「再一次认识」，这个名词正指这第二次认识。

senses.title: The acceptance of a fact
senses.definition: the act of admitting that something is true or official
senses.definitionCN: 承认某事为真或为官方事实的行为
senses.example: The new state won official recognition.
senses.exampleCN: 这个新国家获得了官方承认。
senses.why: To know again is also to admit what one already knew, so the word covers formal acceptance.
senses.whyCN: 「再一次知道」也是承认自己早已知道的事，因此这个词涵盖正式承认。

senses.title: Public praise
senses.definition: the appreciation and honour that a person or a work receives from others
senses.definitionCN: 一个人或一部作品从他人那里得到的欣赏与荣誉
senses.example: She received recognition for her research.
senses.exampleCN: 她的研究获得了认可。
senses.why: When a group knows a person's worth again and again, that knowledge becomes honour.
senses.whyCN: 当一个群体一次次看见某个人的价值，这种认识就变成荣誉。

senses.title: Matching by machine
senses.definition: the process by which a computer identifies a face, a voice, or a pattern
senses.definitionCN: 计算机辨认面孔、声音或图案的过程
senses.example: The system uses facial recognition to unlock the door.
senses.exampleCN: 系统用人脸识别来开门。
senses.why: A machine that matches a pattern knows it again, so the old word fits the new technology.
senses.whyCN: 能匹配图案的机器，就是「再一次认出」它，于是旧词恰好适用于新技术。

intro.en: Recognition is the noun of knowing again: a face, a fact, a person's worth, and a digital pattern.
intro.cn: recognition 是「再次认识」的名词：一张脸、一个事实、一个人的价值，以及一段数字图案。

items.en: Cognoscere meant to know or learn, the root of cognition and recognition.
items.cn: cognoscere 意为认识或得知，是 cognition 与 recognition 的词根。

items.en: Recognoscere added re-, again, to cognoscere, giving the sense of knowing again.
items.cn: recognoscere 在 cognoscere 前加 re-（再次），得到「再一次认识」。

items.en: Recognitio named the act of calling something back to mind.
items.cn: recognitio 指把某物重新唤回心里的行为。

items.en: Old French reconnaissance carried the word into English as a survey or a knowing again.
items.cn: 古法语 reconnaissance 把这个词带入英语，指勘察或再次确认。

items.en: Modern English uses recognition for memory, for diplomacy, for honour, and for machine matching.
items.cn: 现代英语用 recognition 表记忆、外交、荣誉，以及机器匹配。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers nouns ending in the same sound; the near-meaning group gathers words for identification and approval.
note.cn: 形近组收结尾音相同的名词；近义组收表辨认与认可的词。

entries.definition: The mental process of knowing.
A firm belief or a court ruling.
The starting of a fire or engine.
The act of naming what something is.
The act of admitting or thanking.
The act of receiving something as valid.
Recognition of value or quality.

normalIntro.en: The word is knowing plus again: the second knowing is recognition.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是「知道」加「再一次」：第二次知道，就是 recognition。

normal.en: Cognition is knowing; recognition is knowing again.
normal.cn: cognition 是知道，recognition 是再一次知道。

normal.en: Beyond recognition means changed so much that you cannot know it again.
normal.cn: beyond recognition 意为变化太大，再也认不出来。

normal.en: In recognition of is the phrase on a prize or a certificate.
normal.cn: in recognition of 是奖状上的常用短语。

normal.en: Facial recognition is a machine doing the knowing again.
normal.cn: facial recognition 是机器在做「再一次知道」。

normal.en: Keep the g in the middle: recognition, not recongition.
normal.cn: 中间的 g 要保留：recognition，而不是 recongition。

abstract.en: Recognition is the moment when the past and the present meet in one look.
abstract.cn: 认出，是过去与当下在一个目光里相遇的瞬间。

abstract.en: To be recognized is to be told that one's existence counts.
abstract.cn: 被认出，就是被告知自己的存在算数。

abstract.en: A machine that recognizes faces is learning the oldest human act.
abstract.cn: 识别人脸的机器，正在学习最古老的人类行为。

examples.en: He stared at her without recognition.
examples.cn: 他盯着她，却没有认出她。

examples.en: The new state won official recognition.
examples.cn: 这个新国家获得了官方承认。

examples.en: She received recognition for her research.
examples.cn: 她的研究获得了认可。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（再）加 cognition（认知）：再一次认出，就是 recognition——认出、承认、赏识都由此而来。

root: 拉丁 cognoscere（认识）→ recognoscere（再认识）→ recognitio（认出）→ 古法语 reconnaissance → 英语 recognition；同族有 recognize、recognizable。

sensesIntro.en: The core is knowing again; the senses move from a face to a fact, to honour, and to a machine match.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「再一次认识」；义项从一张脸，到事实，到荣誉，再到机器匹配。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a camera sweeping a face, a name appearing on the screen.
core.cn: 核心意象：摄像头扫过脸庞，屏幕上跳出名字。

branches.en: a friend seen across a street
branches.cn: 在街对面看见朋友

branches.en: a treaty signed by two states
branches.cn: 两国签署的条约

branches.en: a medal placed in a hand
branches.cn: 把奖章放进一只手里

branches.en: a screen showing a name
branches.cn: 屏幕上显示的名字

branches.en: a human and a machine both knowing again
branches.cn: 人与机器都在「再一次认识」

intro.en: The word is built on the Latin verb of knowing, with a prefix of repetition and a noun ending of result.
intro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语的「认识」动词上，加上表重复的前缀与表结果的名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is cognoscere, to know, changed by re- and named by -itio.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根是 cognoscere（认识），由 re- 加以改变，并由 -itio 名词化。

core_image: 街上有人叫住你，你回头认出是老同学
scene: 街上有人叫住你，你回头看了两秒才认出对方。I did not recognize him until he called my name.
sceneCN: 这里 recognize 是「认出」（第 1 个义项：认出认识的人或物）；句意为直到他叫我的名字，我才认出他。画面里可留意：回头张望、叫住你的那只手。

senses.title: To know someone again
senses.definition: to identify a person or a thing as one already known
senses.definitionCN: 把某人或某物辨认出为已知对象
senses.example: I did not recognize him until he called my name.
senses.exampleCN: 直到他叫我的名字，我才认出他。
senses.why: Recognoscere meant to know again, and the English verb keeps that moment of a second meeting.
senses.whyCN: recognoscere 意为「再一次认识」，英语动词保留了「第二次相遇」的瞬间。

senses.title: To admit a fact
senses.definition: to accept that something is true, often reluctantly
senses.definitionCN: 接受某事为真，常带不情愿
senses.example: The government finally recognized the problem.
senses.exampleCN: 政府终于承认了这个问题。
senses.why: To know again is also to admit what one already knew, so the word covers reluctant acceptance.
senses.whyCN: 「再一次知道」也是承认自己早已知道的事，因此这个词涵盖不情愿的接受。

senses.title: To give credit
senses.definition: to show appreciation for a person's work or value
senses.definitionCN: 对某人的工作或价值表示欣赏
senses.example: Her work was recognized by the committee.
senses.exampleCN: 她的工作得到了委员会的认可。
senses.why: When others know a person's worth again and again, that knowing becomes public credit.
senses.whyCN: 当他人一次次看见某个人的价值，这种认识就成了公开的认可。

senses.title: To match a pattern by machine
senses.definition: to identify a face, a voice, or a shape by computer
senses.definitionCN: 由计算机辨认面孔、声音或形状
senses.example: The app can recognize handwriting.
senses.exampleCN: 这款应用能识别人手写的字。
senses.why: A machine that matches a pattern knows it again, so the old verb fits the new technology.
senses.whyCN: 能匹配图案的机器，就是「再一次认出」它，于是旧动词恰好适用于新技术。

intro.en: Recognize is the Latin verb of knowing again, carried through French and given an English spelling.
intro.cn: recognize 是拉丁语「再一次认识」的动词，经法语传来，并换上英语拼写。

items.en: Cognoscere meant to know or learn, the root of the whole family.
items.cn: cognoscere 意为认识或得知，是整个词族的词根。

items.en: Recognoscere added re-, again, giving the sense of knowing a second time.
items.cn: recognoscere 加上 re-（再次），得到「第二次认识」。

items.en: Old French carried the verb into English with the same re- prefix.
items.cn: 古法语把这个动词带入英语，re- 前缀保持不变。

items.en: Middle English recognizen covered both identifying and admitting.
items.cn: 中古英语 recognizen 既指辨认，也指承认。

items.en: American spelling settled on -ize, while British English also accepts -ise.
items.cn: 美式拼写定为 -ize，英式英语也接受 -ise。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers verbs ending in the same sound; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of identifying and approving.
note.cn: 形近组收结尾音相同的动词；近义组收表辨认与认可的词。

entries.definition: To arrange something in a new way.
To become aware of something.
To judge faults in something.
To say what something is.
To admit or thank.
To accept a truth unwillingly.
To recognize the value of something.

normalIntro.en: The word is knowing plus again, and the same act covers a face, a fact, a person's value, and a pattern.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是「知道」加「再一次」，同一个行为覆盖一张脸、一个事实、一个人的价值，以及一段图案。

normal.en: Recognize is cognition with a re- in front and an -ize on the end.
normal.cn: recognize 就是 cognition 前面加 re-，后面加 -ize。

normal.en: Recognize a face is the picture; recognize a fact is the extension.
normal.cn: recognize a face 是画面，recognize a fact 是引申。

normal.en: Widely recognized is a common phrase on a plaque or a report.
normal.cn: widely recognized 是奖牌或报告上的常见说法。

normal.en: British English also writes recognise, with s instead of z.
normal.cn: 英式英语也写作 recognise，用 s 代替 z。

normal.en: Do not drop the g: recognize, recognized, recognizing.
normal.cn: 不要漏掉 g：recognize、recognized、recognizing。

abstract.en: To recognize is to let the past prove that it still lives.
abstract.cn: 认出，就是让过去证明它仍然活着。

abstract.en: Recognizing a fault is the first honest act a person can perform.
abstract.cn: 承认错误，是一个人能做的第一件诚实之事。

abstract.en: The one who recognizes another gives that person a place in the world.
abstract.cn: 认出他人的人，等于给了对方一个在世界上的一席之地。

examples.en: I did not recognize him until he called my name.
examples.cn: 直到他叫我的名字，我才认出他。

examples.en: The government finally recognized the problem.
examples.cn: 政府终于承认了这个问题。

examples.en: The app can recognize handwriting.
examples.cn: 这款应用能识别人手写的字。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（再）加 cognize（认识）：再认识一次，就是认出；把已知的事实再确认，就是承认。

root: 拉丁 cognoscere（认识）→ recognoscere（再认识）→ 中古英语 recognizen → 英语 recognize；同族有 recognition、recognizable。

sensesIntro.en: The core is knowing again; the senses move from a face to a fact, to public credit, and to a machine match.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「再一次认识」；义项从一张脸，到事实，到公开认可，再到机器匹配。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stranger calling your name, and a face becoming familiar.
core.cn: 核心意象：陌生人叫出你的名字，一张脸忽然变得熟悉。

branches.en: a face turning in the street
branches.cn: 街上一张转过来的脸

branches.en: a report admitting a fault
branches.cn: 一份承认过错的报告

branches.en: a prize handed over
branches.cn: 递到手上的奖

branches.en: an app reading handwriting
branches.cn: 应用读出手写的字

branches.en: a person known and a person honoured
branches.cn: 认出一个也表彰一个人

intro.en: The Latin verb of knowing takes a prefix of repetition and an English verb ending, and the spellings vary by region.
intro.cn: 拉丁语的「认识」动词接上表重复的前缀与英语动词词尾，拼写因地区而异。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is cognoscere, and re- marks the second knowing; the ending -ize came through French and English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根是 cognoscere，re- 标记第二次认识；词尾 -ize 经法语与英语形成。

definition_zh: 推荐；建议；使显得可取；托付
definition_en: to praise something as worth choosing; to advise a course of action; to make something attractive; to entrust formally
core_image: 店员把一本书递到顾客手里，说值得一读
scene: 书店里，店员从架上抽出一本小说递到顾客手里。Librarians often recommend books to new readers.
sceneCN: 这里 recommend 是「推荐」（第 1 个义项：称赞某物值得选择）；句意为图书管理员常向新读者推荐书籍。画面里可留意：递到手里的书、架上的书脊。

pos.zh: 推荐；建议；使显得可取；托付

senses.title: To praise as worth choosing
senses.definition: to speak in favour of something and suggest that others choose it
senses.definitionCN: 称赞某物并建议他人选择它
senses.example: Librarians often recommend books to new readers.
senses.exampleCN: 图书管理员常向新读者推荐书籍。
senses.why: Commendare meant to praise and entrust, and re- strengthened the praise, so the word pictures praise offered for a choice.
senses.whyCN: commendare 意为称赞与托付，re- 加强了称赞，因此这个词描绘为供人选择而给出的赞美。

senses.title: To advise a course of action
senses.definition: to tell someone what you think they should do
senses.definitionCN: 告诉某人你认为他应当怎么做
senses.example: Doctors recommend regular exercise.
senses.exampleCN: 医生建议经常锻炼。
senses.why: Praise and advice are close: what is worth choosing is also what one should do.
senses.whyCN: 称赞与建议很接近：值得选择的东西，也正是应当去做的事。

senses.title: To make something attractive
senses.definition: to give a place or a plan qualities that invite approval
senses.definitionCN: 赋予某地或某方案令人赞许的品质
senses.example: The quiet garden recommends the house to buyers.
senses.exampleCN: 安静的花园让这所房子更讨买家喜欢。
senses.why: When a place or a plan makes itself pleasing, it is as if it praised itself, and the verb covers that self-praise.
senses.whyCN: 当某地或某方案显得讨人喜欢，它就像在自我称赞，这个动词正涵盖这种自我推荐。

senses.title: To entrust formally
senses.definition: to hand a person or a task into someone's care with confidence
senses.definitionCN: 放心地把人或任务交给他人照管
senses.example: She recommended her children to her sister's care.
senses.exampleCN: 她把孩子托付给姐姐照看。
senses.why: The Latin root also carried the sense of entrusting, because praising someone is a way of handing a task to them.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根也带「托付」义，因为称赞某人，正是把任务交给他的方式。

intro.en: Recommend joins praise to trust: the Latin verb meant both to commend and to entrust, and English kept both directions.
intro.cn: recommend 把称赞与信任连在一起：拉丁动词既指称赞也指托付，英语保留了这两个方向。

items.en: Mandare meant to hand over or command, the root of the whole family.
items.cn: mandare 意为交出或命令，是整个词族的词根。

items.en: Commendare joined com- with mandare and meant to entrust or praise.
items.cn: commendare 由 com- 与 mandare 组成，意为托付或称赞。

items.en: Recommendare strengthened the praise with re- and meant to recommend.
items.cn: recommendare 用 re- 加强称赞，意为推荐。

items.en: French recommander carried the word into English with both senses.
items.cn: 法语 recommander 把称赞与托付两义一起带入英语。

items.en: Modern English added the sense of a place or plan that makes itself attractive.
items.cn: 现代英语又加入了「某地或方案自我推荐」的用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers verbs built on the same Latin root; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of advising and endorsing.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词根上的动词；近义组收表建议与支持的动词。

entries.definition: To praise formally.
To order with authority.
To ask for forcefully.
To put forward an idea.
To tell someone what is wise.
To put forward a plan.
To declare public support.

normalIntro.en: The word is a second praising: re- adds strength to commend, and praise becomes a suggestion.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是「再一次称赞」：re- 为 commend 加强语气，称赞于是变成建议。

normal.en: Re plus commend: praise something twice, and you recommend it.
normal.cn: re 加 commend：把某物称赞两次，就是推荐它。

normal.en: Recommend doing is the pattern; recommend to do is not standard.
normal.cn: recommend doing 是固定结构，recommend to do 不合标准。

normal.en: Highly recommended means many people praise it.
normal.cn: highly recommended 意为很多人称赞它。

normal.en: A doctor recommends a habit; a friend recommends a film.
normal.cn: 医生建议一种习惯，朋友推荐一部电影。

normal.en: Keep the double m: re + commend gives recommend.
normal.cn: 注意双写 m：re 加 commend 构成 recommend。

abstract.en: To recommend is to lend your own judgment to another person.
abstract.cn: 推荐，就是把自己的判断借给别人。

abstract.en: A recommendation is a small promise that the other person will not regret it.
abstract.cn: 推荐是一个小小的承诺：对方不会后悔。

abstract.en: What we recommend reveals what we value more than what we say.
abstract.cn: 我们推荐什么，比我们说什么更能暴露我们的价值。

examples.en: Librarians often recommend books to new readers.
examples.cn: 图书管理员常向新读者推荐书籍。

examples.en: Doctors recommend regular exercise.
examples.cn: 医生建议经常锻炼。

examples.en: The quiet garden recommends the house to buyers.
examples.cn: 安静的花园让这所房子更讨买家喜欢。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（再）加 commend（称赞）：一再称赞，就是推荐；把值得的东西说给别人听，也就是建议。

root: 拉丁 mandare（托付）→ commendare（称赞、托付）→ recommendare（推荐）→ 法语 recommander → 英语 recommend；同族有 recommendation。

sensesIntro.en: The core is praise offered to guide a choice; the senses move from praising a thing to advising an act, to self-praise, and to formal entrusting.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「为引导选择而给出的称赞」；义项从称赞某物，到建议行动，到自我推荐，再到正式托付。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a book taken from a shelf and placed in another person's hands.
core.cn: 核心意象：从架上抽出一本书，放进另一个人手里。

branches.en: a book handed across a counter
branches.cn: 从柜台递过来的一本书

branches.en: a doctor naming a habit
branches.cn: 医生说出一种习惯

branches.en: a garden that sells itself
branches.cn: 一座自我推销的花园

branches.en: children placed in a sister's care
branches.cn: 孩子被托付给姐姐照看

branches.en: praise and advice in one act
branches.cn: 称赞与建议合为一个动作

intro.en: The family is built on a Latin verb of handing over, and praise grows out of the act of entrusting.
intro.cn: 这个词族建立在拉丁语表「交出」的动词上，称赞从托付这一行为中生长出来。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is mandare, to hand over; com- and re- shape it into commend and recommend.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根是 mandare（交出）；com- 与 re- 把它塑造成 commend 与 recommend。

definition_zh: 推荐；建议；推荐信
definition_en: a suggestion that something is worth choosing; a letter praising a person; formal advice in a report
core_image: 教授在办公桌上写一封带签名的信
scene: 教授坐在办公桌旁，把写好的信装进信封，签上名字。She wrote a letter of recommendation for her student.
sceneCN: 这里 recommendation 是「推荐信」（第 2 个义项：为某人说好话的书面材料）；句意为她为学生写了一封推荐信。画面里可留意：桌上的信纸、签好的名字。

senses.title: A suggestion to choose
senses.definition: a piece of advice that something is worth choosing or doing
senses.definitionCN: 认为某物值得选择或某事值得做的一条建议
senses.example: The committee made several recommendations.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会提出了若干建议。
senses.why: The noun turns the act of praising into a piece of advice that another person can follow.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词把称赞的行为变成一条他人可以照做的建议。

senses.title: A letter of praise
senses.definition: a written statement praising a person's qualities, usually for a job or a school
senses.definitionCN: 称赞某人品质的书面材料，通常用于求职或升学
senses.example: She wrote a letter of recommendation for her student.
senses.exampleCN: 她为学生写了一封推荐信。
senses.why: When praise is written down and signed, it becomes a document that travels without its author.
senses.whyCN: 当称赞被写下并签名，它就成了一份能脱离作者而流转的文件。

senses.title: Formal advice in a report
senses.definition: an official proposal made by a committee, an inspector, or a report
senses.definitionCN: 由委员会、检查员或报告提出的正式提议
senses.example: The report's recommendations were accepted by the board.
senses.exampleCN: 报告的建议被董事会采纳了。
senses.why: A committee that praises a policy in public is making a formal recommendation, and the word widened to official advice.
senses.whyCN: 委员会公开称赞某项政策，就是在提出正式建议，于是这个词扩展到官方意见。

intro.en: Recommendation is recommend plus the noun ending -ation: praise and advice turned into a thing one can hold.
intro.cn: recommendation 是 recommend 加名词词尾 -ation：称赞与建议变成了可以拿在手里的东西。

items.en: Mandare meant to hand over, the root behind the whole family.
items.cn: mandare 意为交出，是整个词族背后的词根。

items.en: Commendare joined praise to entrusting, giving both senses to the family.
items.cn: commendare 把称赞与托付结合，为词族带来两层含义。

items.en: The English verb recommend carries praise into a suggestion.
items.cn: 英语动词 recommend 把称赞带入建议。

items.en: The noun ending -ation marks the act or the result of recommending.
items.cn: 名词词尾 -ation 标记推荐的行为或结果。

items.en: Modern English uses the noun for personal advice, for letters, and for official reports.
items.cn: 现代英语用这个名词指个人建议、推荐信，以及官方报告。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers long nouns with the same ending; the near-meaning group gathers words for advice and support.
note.cn: 形近组收结尾相同的长名词；近义组收表建议与支持的词。

entries.definition: Formal praise for someone.
Written material that proves or explains.
A place to stay or a adjustment.
An idea put forward for consideration.
Guidance about what to do.
A formal plan put forward.
Public support for something.

normalIntro.en: The word is recommend plus ation: the act of praising becomes a suggestion, a letter, or a report.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 recommend 加 ation：称赞的行为变成建议、信件或报告。

normal.en: Recommend plus -ation: the thing that is recommended, or the act itself.
normal.cn: recommend 加 -ation：被推荐的东西，或推荐这一行为。

normal.en: A letter of recommendation is a praise that can be carried away.
normal.cn: letter of recommendation 是一份可以带走的称赞。

normal.en: On the recommendation of means because someone advised it.
normal.cn: on the recommendation of 意为根据某人的建议。

normal.en: Make a recommendation is the formal way to say give advice.
normal.cn: make a recommendation 是「提出建议」的正式说法。

normal.en: The plural adds s: recommendations, with no change in the stem.
normal.cn: 复数加 s：recommendations，词干不变。

abstract.en: A recommendation is a piece of another person's judgment you are allowed to borrow.
abstract.cn: 一条建议，是你被允许借用的他人判断。

abstract.en: Written praise outlives the voice that spoke it.
abstract.cn: 写下的称赞，比说出它的声音活得更久。

abstract.en: Every recommendation carries the risk of being wrong in public.
abstract.cn: 每一条建议，都承担着公开出错的风险。

examples.en: The committee made several recommendations.
examples.cn: 委员会提出了若干建议。

examples.en: She wrote a letter of recommendation for her student.
examples.cn: 她为学生写了一封推荐信。

examples.en: The report's recommendations were accepted by the board.
examples.cn: 报告的建议被董事会采纳了。

dict_mnemonic.text: recommend（推荐）加 ation（行为、结果）：推荐这一行为，以及推荐所形成的东西——建议、推荐信。

root: recommend（推荐）+ 后缀 -ation（行为或结果）→ recommendation；recommend 源自拉丁 recommendare；同族有 recommendable。

sensesIntro.en: The core is praise made usable; the senses move from advice, to a signed letter, to a formal report.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「可用的称赞」；义项从建议，到签名信，再到正式报告。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a signed letter placed in an envelope on a desk.
core.cn: 核心意象：办公桌上，一封签好名的信被装进信封。

branches.en: a short list of good options
branches.cn: 一张写着好选项的短清单

branches.en: a letter sealed in an envelope
branches.cn: 封进信封的信

branches.en: a report read aloud at a meeting
branches.cn: 会上被朗读的报告

branches.en: advice spoken and advice written
branches.cn: 口头的建议与书面的建议

branches.en: a personal letter and an official report
branches.cn: 一封私人信件与一份官方报告

intro.en: The word adds a noun ending to the verb of praise, and the result names advice, a letter, and a report.
intro.cn: 这个词在表称赞的动词上加名词词尾，结果便指建议、信件与报告。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is mandare, to hand over; com- and re- shape the verb, and -ation names its result.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根是 mandare（交出）；com- 与 re- 塑造动词，-ation 命名其结果。

definition_zh: 和解；调和；使一致；对账；使顺从
definition_en: to bring people, ideas or records back into agreement after a difference
core_image: 两本账簿摊在桌上，数字一格一格对上，最后一行终于写出同一个合计
scene: 交报表前，她把发票、银行流水和台账逐笔核对，找出差了的那两笔。She reconciled the two records before submitting the report.
sceneCN: 这里指把两套记录核对到一致（第 4 个义项：核对账目使相符）；句意为她在交报表前把两套记录对平了。图中可辨识物件：摊开的账簿、逐行核对的笔迹、写出同一合计的最后一行。

derivatives.zh: 由该动词加表示动作结果的名词尾构成，义为「和解；调和；对账」
由该动词加表示倾向的形容词尾构成，义为「和解性的」
由该动词加表示施动者的名词尾构成，义为「调停者」
由否定前缀加「可调和的」构成，义为「不可调和的」
由该动词加已然词尾构成，义为「已和解的；已对平的」

senses.title: To restore a relationship
senses.definition: to bring two people or groups back to friendly relations after a quarrel
senses.definitionCN: 在争吵之后使人或群体重回友好关系
senses.example: The brothers reconciled after the funeral.
senses.exampleCN: 兄弟俩在葬礼之后和解了。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to bring back together into a council, and that is the human core of the word.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「重新召集到一处」，这正是这个词的人情内核。

senses.title: To harmonise ideas
senses.definition: to show that two apparently opposed ideas can both be accepted
senses.definitionCN: 说明两种看似对立的观点可以同时成立
senses.example: The essay reconciles scientific evidence with local belief.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章把科学证据与当地信仰调和起来。
senses.why: Ideas are brought into one council too, and reconciliation is the seating of opponents at one table.
senses.whyCN: 观点也被召进同一个议事厅，调和就是让对手坐到一张桌子旁。

senses.title: To make statements consistent
senses.definition: to make an account agree with the evidence or with another account
senses.definitionCN: 使一种说法与证据或另一种说法相符
senses.example: He could not reconcile his story with the time stamps.
senses.exampleCN: 他无法让自己的说法与时间戳对上。
senses.why: When two accounts disagree, reconciling them means finding the version that satisfies both.
senses.whyCN: 当两份叙述不一致，调和就是找出能同时满足两者的版本。

senses.title: To check financial records
senses.definition: to compare two sets of records and adjust them until they agree
senses.definitionCN: 比较两套记录并调整到相符
senses.example: The clerk reconciled the bank statement with the ledger.
senses.exampleCN: 职员把银行对账单与台账对平了。
senses.why: Accounting turned the council image into two columns that must arrive at one total.
senses.whyCN: 会计把「议事厅」的画面变成两栏必须合成一个总数的数字。

senses.title: To accept something reluctantly
senses.definition: to bring oneself to accept a difficult situation that cannot be changed
senses.definitionCN: 使自己接受一个无法改变的困难处境
senses.example: She reconciled herself to the longer commute.
senses.exampleCN: 她只好接受了更长的通勤。
senses.why: This reflexive use is a private council: the self is brought back into agreement with reality.
senses.whyCN: 这个反身用法是一场私下的议事：自我被重新与现实达成一致。

senses.title: To mediate a dispute
senses.definition: to act as a third party who brings two sides to an agreement
senses.definitionCN: 作为第三方让两边达成一致
senses.example: A retired judge reconciled the neighbours over the boundary.
senses.exampleCN: 一位退休法官就边界纠纷调解了两家邻居。
senses.why: Mediation is the verb performed on behalf of others rather than on oneself.
senses.whyCN: 调解是替别人而不是替自己行使这个动词。

senses.title: To align two datasets
senses.definition: to match two sets of data that use different formats or identifiers
senses.definitionCN: 把格式或标识不同的两套数据匹配起来
senses.example: The team reconciled the sensor logs with the maintenance records.
senses.exampleCN: 团队把传感器日志与维护记录对齐了。
senses.why: Data work inherited the accounting sense: two systems describe one reality and must be made to agree.
senses.whyCN: 数据工作继承了会计义：两个系统描述同一现实，必须被弄成一致。

senses.title: To balance competing needs
senses.definition: to find a practical arrangement that meets two demands at once
senses.definitionCN: 找到同时满足两项要求的实际安排
senses.example: The plan reconciles housing demand with the need for open land.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方案兼顾了住房需求与保留空地的需要。
senses.why: Planning is a council of demands, and reconciling them is what a plan is for.
senses.whyCN: 规划就是各种需求的议事厅，而调和它们正是方案存在的理由。

intro.en: Reconcile comes from Latin reconciliare, to bring together again, from re-, again, and conciliare, to unite, from concilium, an assembly. English took it through French.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 reconciliare「重新聚到一起」，由 re-「再」与 conciliare「使联合」构成，而 conciliare 出自 concilium「集会」；英语经法语引入。

items.en: Concilium meant an assembly or council, the gathering of people into one body.
items.cn: 这个词意为集会或议事会，即把人聚成一个整体。

items.en: Conciliare meant to unite or to win over, and it could also mean to procure or to cause.
items.cn: 这个词意为使联合、争取过来，也可指取得或促成。

items.en: The prefix meant again or back, so reconciliare pictured a second gathering after a break.
items.cn: 前缀意为「再、回」，所以这个词的画面是破裂之后的第二次聚集。

items.en: The verb meant to restore to friendship or to bring back into agreement.
items.cn: 这个动词意为恢复友好或使重新一致。

items.en: English adopted the verb through French; the exact first date is uncertain and is usually given only as that century.
items.cn: 英语经法语采用这个动词；确切首见年代不确定，通常只给「十四世纪」。

items.en: Bookkeeping gave the verb its ledger sense, in which the two parties are two sets of figures.
items.cn: 记账给这个动词添了账簿义，其中的「两方」变成了两套数字。

note.en: The first group shares the council stem or looks close; the second group names neighbouring ideas of agreement and settlement.
note.cn: 第一组与「reconcile」共享「集会」词干或只是形近；第二组是与「一致、解决」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The noun for the act of restoring agreement.
entries.definitionCN: 指恢复一致这一行为的名词。

entries.definition: An adjective for differences that cannot be settled.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指无法调和的分歧。

entries.definition: To win over or pacify, from the same council verb without the re-.
entries.definitionCN: 指安抚、争取，同出「集会」动词，只是没有表示「再」的前缀。

entries.definition: A governing assembly, from the same Latin noun but a different spelling path.
entries.definitionCN: 指议事机构，同出同一拉丁名词，但拼写路径不同。

entries.definition: Advice or a legal adviser, from a different Latin verb meaning to consult.
entries.definitionCN: 指建议或法律顾问，出自另一个表示「商议」的拉丁动词。

entries.definition: To end a dispute by agreement, the plainest verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指以协议结束争端，最朴素的说法。

entries.definition: To fix a problem or decide firmly.
entries.definitionCN: 指解决问题或下定决心。

entries.definition: To make parts fit together without conflict.
entries.definitionCN: 指使各部分协调不冲突。

entries.definition: To stand between two sides and help them agree.
entries.definitionCN: 指居于两方之间帮助他们达成一致。

entries.definition: To bring things into the same line, often used of data.
entries.definitionCN: 指把事物排到同一条线上，常用于数据。

entries.definition: To repair a relationship roughly and quickly.
entries.definitionCN: 指粗略快速地修复关系。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the council inside the word, the accountant's ledger, and the spelling trap with counsel.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用词里的「集会」、会计的账簿，以及 counsel 这个拼写陷阱。

normal.en: Concilium is a council, so reconcile is to call everyone back to one table.
normal.cn: concilium 是议事会，所以这个词就是把人都叫回一张桌子。

normal.en: The re- means again, so the word always implies a break that came first.
normal.cn: re- 意为「再」，所以这个词总暗含先前的一次破裂。

normal.en: Accountants reconcile two sets of figures until they agree.
normal.cn: 会计把两套数字对到相符为止。

normal.en: Reconcile oneself to a hard fact is a private version of the same table.
normal.cn: 让自己接受一个硬事实，是同一张桌子的私下版本。

normal.en: Council is the assembly, counsel is advice, and only council belongs here.
normal.cn: council 是议事机构，counsel 是建议，只有前者与这个词相关。

abstract.en: To reconcile is not to prove one side right; it is to build a table both can sit at.
abstract.cn: 调和不是证明某一方正确，而是造一张双方都能坐下的桌子。

abstract.en: Two true accounts can still disagree, and the work is to find why.
abstract.cn: 两份真实的叙述仍可能对不上，而工作就是找出为什么。

abstract.en: The hardest reconciliation is the one a person performs with a fact that will not move.
abstract.cn: 最难的和解，是一个人跟一个不会改变的事实之间达成的那个。

examples.en: The two countries reconciled after years of frozen relations.
examples.cn: 多年关系冻结之后，两国和解了。

examples.en: It is hard to reconcile such a claim with the published data.
examples.cn: 这样的说法很难与已发表的数据相符。

examples.en: Please reconcile the invoice total with the purchase order.
examples.cn: 请把发票总额与采购订单核对一致。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「瑞康赛尔」——两本账簿摊开，末行写出同一个数：调和、对账

root: 拉丁语 concilium「集会」→ conciliare「使联合」→ reconciliare「重新聚到一起」（re-「再」）；英语十四世纪经法语引入。与 counsel「建议」不同源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all seat two parties at one table: people, ideas, statements, records, the self, a dispute, datasets and competing needs.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在把两方请到同一张桌子：人、观点、说法、账目、自我、争端、数据集与冲突的需求。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two ledgers lie open, line by line is matched, and one total finally appears at the bottom.
core.cn: 核心意象：两本账簿摊开，逐行对上，最后一行终于写出同一个合计。

branches.en: THE TABLE IS RESET: two people or two groups are brought back to one table, sometimes by a third party.
branches.cn: 桌子被重摆：两个人或两个群体被带回同一桌，有时由第三方促成。

branches.en: THE IDEAS SHARE A ROOM: opposed views or competing needs are arranged so both can stand.
branches.cn: 观点共用一室：对立观点或冲突需求被安排到可以并存。

branches.en: THE STORY IS TESTED: a claim is checked until it fits the evidence.
branches.cn: 说法被检验：一种叙述被核到与证据相符。

branches.en: THE FIGURES MEET: ledgers or datasets are matched until one total appears.
branches.cn: 数字对上：账簿或数据集被匹配到一个总数。

branches.en: THE SELF YIELDS: a person comes to terms with what cannot be changed.
branches.cn: 自我让步：人与无法改变的事达成妥协。

intro.en: Reconcile is a Latin verb of gathering, and its pieces are the prefix of return and the noun for an assembly.
intro.cn: 这是一个表示「聚拢」的拉丁动词，其部件是「返回」的前缀与表示「集会」的名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies concilium, conciliare and reconciliare; the family is well recorded, so no part is marked uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了 concilium、conciliare、reconciliare；这一族有清楚记录，没有哪一部分标为存疑。

items.example: The noun is the room where the parties meet.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是各方会面的那个房间。

items.example: The verb names the act of bringing together.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指把人聚到一起的动作。

items.example: It marks the second gathering after a break.
items.exampleCN: 它标出破裂后的第二次聚集。

items.example: The verb carried both the human and the agreement senses.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词兼有人际与一致两种意义。

items.example: The noun supplied the English word for the process.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词提供了英语中表示过程的名词。

items.example: It forms irreconcilable with an assimilated r.
items.exampleCN: 它与同化的 r 一起构成 irreconcilable。

items.example: It forms the adjective for what can be settled.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示「可调和的」形容词。

derivatives.zh: 由该动词加表示动作结果的名词尾构成，义为「和解；调和；对账」
由该动词加表示倾向的形容词尾构成，义为「和解性的」
由否定前缀加「可调和的」构成，义为「不可调和的」
由该动词加表示施动者的名词尾构成，义为「调停者」

definition_zh: 重建；重建物；复原；（语言学）构拟；重建时期
definition_en: the act or result of building something again, or of piecing together something that is no longer intact
core_image: 散落一地的碎石被按编号重新拼回一座拱门
scene: 这里指「重建」。 The reconstruction took years and twice the original budget to finish.
sceneCN: 这里 reconstruction 指「实体重建」（第 1 个义项：把被毁的结构重新建起）；句意：这座桥的重建用了三年，花费是最初预算的两倍。图中可辨识物件：编号石块、拱门、吊车、图纸。

pos.zh: 重建；重建物；复原；（语言学）构拟；（美国史）重建时期（作专有名词时大写）

senses.title: Rebuilding a damaged structure
senses.titleCN: 实体重建：把被毁的建筑重新建起
senses.definition: the act of building again something that was destroyed or badly damaged
senses.definitionCN: 把被摧毁或严重损坏的事物重新建造起来的行动
senses.example: The reconstruction of the bridge took three years.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥的重建用了三年。
senses.why: The noun joins re- 'again' to construction, from Latin construere 'to pile up together', so it means piling the same structure up once more.
senses.whyCN: 该名词把 re-「再次」与 construction 结合，后者出自拉丁 construere「堆叠在一起」，因此意为把同一结构再堆起来一次。

senses.title: Recreating a past event
senses.titleCN: 事件还原：根据线索复原经过
senses.definition: the act of piecing together what happened from remaining evidence
senses.definitionCN: 根据残存证据把发生过的事情拼合出来
senses.example: Police reconstructed the accident from skid marks and camera footage.
senses.exampleCN: 警方根据刹车痕与监控画面还原了事故经过。
senses.why: The image shifts from stone to evidence: what is rebuilt is no longer a wall but a sequence of events.
senses.whyCN: 意象从石头转向证据：被重建的不再是一堵墙，而是一连串事件。

senses.title: Linguistic reconstruction
senses.titleCN: 语言构拟：由现存语言反推古语形式
senses.definition: in linguistics, the inferred recovery of an earlier language form from its surviving descendants
senses.definitionCN: 语言学中，从现存后代语言反推更早语言形式的做法
senses.example: The reconstruction of Proto-Indo-European rests on systematic sound correspondences.
senses.exampleCN: 原始印欧语的构拟依赖系统的语音对应关系。
senses.why: Linguists reconstruct a lost language the way engineers rebuild a bridge: from fragments, but with rules that constrain the guess.
senses.whyCN: 语言学家构拟已消失的语言，如同工程师重建桥梁：从残片出发，但用规则约束猜测。

senses.title: National rebuilding after war
senses.titleCN: 战后国家重建：修复社会与经济
senses.definition: the large-scale rebuilding of a country's buildings, economy and institutions after war or disaster
senses.definitionCN: 战争或灾难后对一个国家建筑、经济与制度的大规模重建
senses.example: Post-war reconstruction reshaped both the city and its politics.
senses.exampleCN: 战后重建同时重塑了这座城市及其政治。
senses.why: The building metaphor scales up: a nation is treated as a structure whose parts must be raised again together.
senses.whyCN: 建筑隐喻被放大：国家被当成一座结构，其各部分必须再次一起立起。

senses.title: Surgical reconstruction
senses.titleCN: 手术重建：修复身体结构
senses.definition: in medicine, surgery that rebuilds a body part damaged by injury, disease or congenital condition
senses.definitionCN: 医学中指重建因伤、病或先天状况受损的身体部位的手术
senses.example: Reconstruction of her jaw followed the removal of the tumour.
senses.exampleCN: 切除肿瘤之后，她接受了下颌重建手术。
senses.why: Medicine applies the word to flesh: the damaged part is rebuilt rather than merely repaired at the surface.
senses.whyCN: 医学把这个词用于身体：受损部位是被重建，而不只是表面修补。
